title: Pippa and the Splashy Stream
markdown:
Pippa the pony, with her mane the colour of a sunrise – a dazzling pink, mind you! – was as cheerful as a bumblebee in a field of clover. Every happy step she took made her mane bounce and sway. And who was her trusty co-adventurer? None other than Nutmeg the dormouse! This little fellow, with eyes like shiny brown marbles, was perched comfortably on a smooth, grey stone that had cleverly hitched a ride on Pippa’s back. Tucked safely in a tiny, woven basket beside him, filled to the very brim, was the most delicious wildflower honey you ever did smell.

“This honey,” chirped Nutmeg, his voice as light and airy as dandelion fluff, “is absolutely extraordinary! It’s from the very finest wildflowers, gathered with the most patient care and a whisper of moonlight.”

Pippa nodded enthusiastically, her nose twitching with happy anticipation. “And it’s for the Wrigglebottom family! They’re having their annual Blossom Festival today. Oh, Nutmeg, I do hope they’ll think it’s just as special as we do! The festival starts promptly at noon, and the best honey is always served first!”

Delivering treats and bringing smiles to faces was Pippa’s very favourite kind of mission. It made her feel like a true hero of happiness. But as they trotted along the sun-dappled path, a tiny, ticklish flutter began to stir in her tummy. It felt like a tiny, excited butterfly doing loop-the-loops! Just ahead, glinting merrily in the sunshine, was the Whispering Stream. Now, it wasn't a roaring river, oh no. It was quite small, no wider than three of Pippa’s sturdy hoof-prints, but it was new. Pippa had never, ever crossed it before.

“Oh, Nutmeg,” she whispered, her happy trot slowing to a gentle stroll. “Look. The stream. It… it looks terribly… splashy.”

This is worry, she realised, a small cloud of it drifting into her happy thoughts. Her hooves, usually so light and ready for a gallop, felt suddenly very, very heavy, as if they were made of lead. The butterfly in her tummy did a rather dramatic somersault.

Nutmeg, whose sharp eyes missed nothing, tilted his little head. “Splashy, you say? Yes! It sings a joyful song when the water dances over the smooth stones. But don’t you worry your lovely pink mane, Pippa! Remember those sunbeams we chased yesterday? You weren’t worried about them one bit!”

“Sunbeams don’t splash you right on your nose,” Pippa mumbled, her ears drooping just a tiny, almost invisible, bit. The precious basket of honey seemed to grow heavier with every hesitant step.

They reached the very edge of the stream. The water chuckled and gurgled, a playful, bubbly sound that bounced off the pebbles. But Pippa saw her reflection in the water, and oh dear, it was a wobbly pony looking quite uncertain. She imagined her hooves slipping on a wet stone, and her heart gave a little thump.

“Here’s where it gets interesting,” Nutmeg piped up, his whiskers twitching with a spark of an idea. “Here’s a pro tip from someone who’s seen more streams than a duck has feathers: sometimes, the best way across isn’t the most obvious way! Turning back might seem easy, Pippa, but then the Wrigglebottoms won’t get their honey in time!”

He scurried from his comfortable stone-seat onto Pippa’s back, his tiny paws tapping near her ear. “Look! Do you see them? The big, smooth stones! They make a perfect path, don’t they? They don’t wiggle or wobble. They just sit there, solid as a freshly baked biscuit! A real explorer sees the puzzle, Pippa!”

Pippa looked. And she saw! There were indeed several large, flat stones, placed just so, like a series of stepping-stones, forming a clear, dry path right across the water. They looked wonderfully steady, like little islands waiting patiently for her.

“But… but what if I step on one and it wobbles anyway?” Pippa asked, her voice still a little shaky, like a leaf in a gentle breeze.

Nutmeg, brave as a lion (a very, very tiny lion), hopped onto the very first stone. He stood there, testing it with all his might. It didn't budge an inch. “This stone,” he declared proudly, “is as steady as a sleeping hedgehog! And that one,” he pointed a tiny paw to the next, “is as sturdy as a sturdy oak leaf!”

Pippa took a deep, deep breath. The air smelled wonderfully of wildflowers and warm, friendly earth. She could hear the cheerful chirping of meadowlarks high above. This wasn’t a scary, dark place with unknown dangers. It was just… a stream. And she had a very important delivery to make.

“Alright,” she said, her voice gaining a little more confidence, like a small wave growing stronger. “I’ll try. But you keep talking, Nutmeg. Like a very encouraging weather report for bravery!”

Nutmeg giggled, a sound like tiny bells chiming. “Will do! The forecast for Pippa’s bravery is… sunny with a chance of enormous, spectacular courage!”

With Nutmeg cheering from the first solid stone, Pippa carefully, deliberately, stepped onto the second. The stone felt rough and cool beneath her hoof. It held her weight steady. Oh! she thought, a happy little surprise bubbling up inside her. It doesn’t wobble at all! It’s like walking on the meadow floor! She took another step, and then another. The water splashed gently around the stones, making little rainbow-coloured droplets, but it didn’t splash her.

Then came the last stone. It was a little farther away, and as Pippa gathered herself to jump, the water surged and splashed around it, a rainbow mist rising. Pippa felt the spray cool on her nose, heard the gurgling roar, and smelled the damp earth mixing with sweet flower scents. Her heart thumped like a drum against her ribs. To make sure the precious honey stayed safe, she stretched her neck further than she liked, her pink mane catching the breeze. She willingly got a little splash on her nose, a small price to pay for such a grand delivery.

And then, quite suddenly, she was on the other side! The meadow stretched out before her, a carpet of green and gold, and there, not far away at all, were the familiar, cozy burrows of the Wrigglebottom family. A wave of sweet relief, followed by a burst of pure, unadulterated joy, washed over Pippa. Her tummy butterfly was no longer doing worried flips; it was soaring and dancing with happy abandon!

“We did it!” Pippa whinnied, a happy sound that echoed through the meadow like a joyful song.

Mr. and Mrs. Wrigglebottom, along with their littlest bunnies, all with twitching noses and bright eyes, hopped out to greet them. “Pippa! Nutmeg! You’re here! And what a glorious basket of honey you’ve brought!” exclaimed Mrs. Wrigglebottom, her voice full of delight.

As Pippa watched the bunnies dip their tiny spoons into the golden honey, their faces beaming with happiness, she felt a warm, contented glow spread all through her. She had been a little bit scared, yes, that was true. But she had also been incredibly brave. She had listened to her best friend, and she had taken that very first, important, wobbly step.

Later, as they trotted home, the sun casting long, friendly shadows that stretched like sleepy cats, Pippa felt quite different. A small puddle sparkled on the path. Pippa trotted right through it, sending a joyful spray dancing in the air. Just a puddle! she thought, her mane catching the breeze. The Whispering Stream still gurgled and chuckled, but now it sounded like a happy secret being shared.

“That was quite an adventure, wasn’t it, Pippa?” Nutmeg said, snuggled contentedly on his stone-seat.

Pippa nudged him gently with her soft nose. “It was,” she agreed, her voice clear and strong. “And you know what? The stream wasn’t so splashy after all. It was just… a stream. And I am Pippa the pony who crossed it!”

Her bright pink mane seemed to shimmer with an extra sparkle in the fading sunlight. And that little butterfly in her tummy? It was flying higher and freer than ever before.
characters: Pippa the pony, Nutmeg the dormouse
